work.name: Augmodo
work.summary: Uncertainty-aware open-world computer vision for retail deployments, across 100k+ images a day.
highlights: Working alongside Sacha Hu (Senior CV Engineer), Ashley Napier (CV Group Lead), and Galen Han.

Developed uncertainty-aware open-world VLMs that recognize products, aisles, and price tags from images alone, trained on paired images and product descriptions for identification and planogram matching.

Deployed test-time augmentation to quantify confidence in open-world classifiers (product identification, QC automation, RGB+depth empty-shelf detection): confident predictions are auto-accepted and only uncertain ones reach human QC, across 100k+ images/day.
Fine-tuned YOLO and the transformer-based RF-DETR with hard-negative mining and multi-GPU cloud training, improving empty-shelf detection without regressing other shelf classes.
Designed automated relabeling pipelines that update legacy bounding-box annotations at scale, adapting large datasets to newer architectures without manual re-annotation.

work.name: Michelin
work.summary: Conformal and adaptive soft sensors for real-time quality prediction in industrial batch processes.
highlights: Supervised by Dr. Sylvain Desroziers, Dr. Maxime Moreaud, and Guillaume Ramelet.

Introduced Self-Organized Conformal Prediction (NeurIPS 2026): unsupervised group discovery with a Self-Organizing Map for group-local calibration, cutting regional coverage gaps on all 10 datasets, by 14.8% on average, for only 3% larger prediction sets.

Co-developed Mask-Valid Conformal Prediction (with M. Hegazy, M. I. Jordan, A. Dieuleveut): binary monitoring masks that interpolate between marginal and anytime coverage, with restart validity after failures and no need for past test labels.

Created and open-sourced TorchSOM (JMLR 2026), a PyTorch library for Self-Organizing Maps: 74-98% faster than MiniSom on CPU, about 8× faster than somoclu on GPU, and the lowest topographic error in every benchmark (34-81% below MiniSom).

Developed adaptive Just-in-Time soft sensors pairing SOM similarity retrieval with online SHAP feature selection, cutting MSE by up to 61% over global baselines (IEEE ETFA 2026) and prediction error by over 90% under year-long drift on 35k production batches.

Built an explainable, uncertainty-aware analytics framework (frequency-ranked feature selection, SHAP interactions, multi-split conformal prediction) on 35k rubber-mixing records, cutting 316 input variables to 20 at equal accuracy (Digital Chemical Engineering 2026).

highlights: Taught the fundamentals of machine learning, from data preprocessing and feature engineering to model training and evaluation, under Pr. Philippe Xu.
Guided students through their first hands-on experience building and validating predictive models.

work.name: Adaptive & Intelligent Robotics Lab (AIRL)
work.summary: Sample-efficient Quality-Diversity optimization using surrogate models for robotic control in uncertain environments.
highlights: Supervised by Pr. Antoine Cully.
Tackled the data-hunger of MAP-Elites by integrating probabilistic surrogate models on a robotic arm control task; the best variant beat MAP-Elites and came close to MAP-Elites with sampling.
Benchmarked eight algorithmic variants combining different surrogate architectures and acquisition strategies in non-deterministic environments.
Introduced two metrics for the uncertainty of quality-diversity archives.

work.name: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (CNRS)
work.summary: Deep learning for detecting fast ripples, pathological biomarkers for epileptic tissue, in intracranial EEG signals.
highlights: Supervised by Dr. Ludovic Gardy, Pr. Christophe Hurter, and Pr. Emmanuel Barbeau.
Trained CNN fast-ripple detectors on wavelet time-frequency images of macro- and micro-electrode EEG, improving accuracy by 5% through systematic hyperparameter tuning (J. Neurosci. Methods 2025).
Applied Grad-CAM to localize high-frequency bursts in time-frequency maps, giving clinicians visual explanations anchored to known fast-ripple signatures.
Accelerated EEG signal and image processing by 15% with Cython, and built 7 NoSQL databases for multi-channel EEG at macro and micro electrode scales for batch retrieval and parallel processing.

work.name: EuroMov Digital Health in Motion (DHM)
work.summary: Anisotropic image filtering for sub-pixel accurate line feature detection, published at IEEE ICASSP 2023.
highlights: Supervised by Pr. Baptiste Magnier and Pr. Binbin Xu.
Designed the 2D Semi Bi-Gaussian (2DSBG) filter, an asymmetric convolution kernel that enhances elongated structures while suppressing isotropic noise.
Benchmarked against state-of-the-art edge detection models (DexiNed, RCF, Laplacian-of-Gaussian) on synthetic and real-world datasets.
